mainTopic: Wording of conditional and time-based גיטין, the end of פרק מי שאחזו, and the opening of פרק הזורק on a גט thrown into the wife's domain.
overview: The עמוד first finishes the discussion of a גט tied to sunrise. 'When the sun comes out' starts only in the morning, so it fails if the husband dies at night. 'On condition' works from now. The תנאים argue only about 'if,' depending on רבי יוסי's rule that a document's date shows when it starts. Next, רב אשי explains that רבי יוסי validates the twelve-month case only because the husband said 'write and give if I do not come,' which means 'write now.' A ברייתא then teaches how much time the word 'after' adds to a period. The גמרא explains 'after שבת' and shows that רבי's 'thirty days after the רגל' is not the הלכה. Then פרק מי שאחזו ends, and the new פרק opens with a משנה about throwing a גט into the wife's domain. The גמרא learns this from ״ונתן״, compares it to a גנב, and explains why both sources are needed. Finally it asks how a wife can own a courtyard, and answers that the husband gave up his rights while she was still an ארוסה. A support from רבא begins at the end and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: 'When the sun comes out' starts only in the morning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the wording לכשתצא ('when it comes out') makes the גט start only at sunrise, so if the husband dies at night, it would be a גט after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: With 'when it comes out,' he is telling her the גט starts once the sun comes out. So if he dies during the night, it would be a גט that starts after his death, and that does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining why the wording 'when the sun comes out' does not make a valid גט if the husband dies during the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'when' points to a future starting time: the גט begins only at sunrise. A גט cannot take effect after the husband has died. So if he dies before morning, the גט comes too late and is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: When it comes out. The גט starts only at that future moment.
A גט that would take effect after the husband's death, which is never valid

phrases.english: He is saying to her: once it comes out,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the sun; this explains the words 'when the sun comes out' from just before.

phrases.english: and if he dies during the night,
it is a bill of divorce after death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous עמוד by explaining the 'when' wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'When the sun comes out' means the גט starts only at sunrise. If the husband dies at night, it is a גט after death and is invalid.

steps.title: 'On condition' works retroactively from now
steps.stepSummary: The wording על מנת ('on condition') means the גט takes effect from now once the condition is met, based on רב הונא in the name of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But 'on condition that the sun comes out of its sheath' means he is telling her the גט works from now. As רב הונא said in the name of רב: anyone who says 'on condition' is like someone who says 'from now.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא contrasts 'on condition' with 'when.' It explains that 'on condition' makes the גט work from right now, and it backs this up with a rule of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With על מנת, the גט starts at the moment it is given, and sunrise only confirms it. So even if the husband dies at night, the גט already took effect while he was alive. רב's general rule is the source: 'on condition' always means 'from now.'

keyTerms.meaning: The sun from its sheath. A picture for sunrise.
From now. The deal starts right away once the condition is met.

steps.whyThisMatters: רב's rule that 'on condition' equals 'from now' is a basic tool that the גמרא uses across many topics of conditional deals.

phrases.english: 'On condition that the sun will emerge from its sheath':
he is saying to her: from now,
as Rav Huna said that Rav said:
Anyone who says 'on condition'
is like one who says 'from now.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to step 1: a wording that does work even if he dies at night.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'On condition' means 'from now,' so the גט is valid even if the husband dies before sunrise.

steps.title: The real dispute is only over the word 'if'
steps.stepSummary: The תנאים disagree only about אם תצא ('if it comes out'). One side follows רבי יוסי (the date proves when it starts). The other side does not, so for them it is a plain 'if I die.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagreed about 'if it comes out.' One master holds like רבי יוסי, who says the date on a document proves when it starts. So it is like saying 'from today if I die,' or 'from now if I die.' The other master does not hold like רבי יוסי, so it is just a plain 'if I die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down exactly where the תנאים argue: only in the 'if' wording. It explains each side by whether they follow רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'If' is unclear: does the גט start now, or only later? For רבי יוסי, the date written on the גט shows it starts on that day, so 'if' works like 'from today,' and the גט is valid. Without רבי יוסי's rule, 'if' is like a plain 'if I die,' which would be a גט after death and does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: If it comes out. The unclear wording.
The date of a document proves when it takes effect (רבי יוסי's rule)
One master… the other master. A way of naming the two sides of a dispute.

steps.whatToRemember: Three wordings: 'when' (לכשתצא) is not valid if he dies at night. 'On condition' (על מנת) is valid, because it means 'from now.' 'If' (אם) depends on רבי יוסי: the date on the גט makes it like 'from today.'
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the dispute is about whether a גט can work after death. Everyone agrees it cannot. They only argue whether the word 'if' makes the גט start now or later.

phrases.english: They disagreed only about 'if it comes out':
one master holds like Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: This is the side called 'our Rabbis,' who said the גט is valid.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: זְמַנּוֹ שֶׁל שְׁטָר מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו,
phrases.english: who says: the date of a document proves about it,
so it is like 'from today if I die,'
like 'from now if I die';
the other master does not hold like Rabbi Yosei,
so it is like a plain 'if I die.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the 'when' and 'on condition' cases, it narrows the dispute to the remaining 'if' case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement is only over 'if.' Those who follow רבי יוסי's rule about the date treat it like 'from today' and validate the גט. Those who reject that rule treat it as a plain 'if I die,' which is invalid.

steps.title: New section: the husband who may not return within twelve months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of a new משנה: a husband tells people to write and give a גט to his wife if he does not come back within twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Write and give a גט to my wife if I do not come back from now until twelve months': if they wrote it, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the opening words of the משנה. It is setting up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה says they wrote the גט within the twelve months but gave it to her only after. The first opinion says it is not valid, and רבי יוסי says it is valid. The גמרא quotes just the first words to show which case it is about to discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: Write and give. The husband's instruction to agents.
And so on. Short for the rest of the quote.

phrases.english: 'Write and give a bill of divorce to my wife,
if I do not come back from now
until twelve months':
if they wrote it, and so on.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: they wrote it within the year but gave it after the year. The first opinion says it's not valid; רבי יוסי says it is.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּתְבוּ וּתְנוּ גֵּט לְאִשְׁתִּי אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִכָּאן וְעַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the sun cases to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the case of a גט written within twelve months but given after them, which the גמרא will now discuss.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי validate any גט written on condition?
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר asks רב אשי whether רבי יוסי holds that a גט written on a condition is valid even before the condition is fulfilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said to רב אשי: Shall we say that רבי יוסי holds that a גט written on condition is valid?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר looks at רבי יוסי's ruling in the משנה and asks whether it shows a broad rule: a גט written before its condition is met is still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the scribes wrote the גט during the twelve months, before it was clear the husband would not return, and רבי יוסי still called it a גט. רב יימר suggests this means רבי יוסי allows writing a גט on condition in general. The next step will reject that broad reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggested conclusion that may be rejected)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar said to Rav Ashi:
Shall we say that Rabbi Yosei holds
if he wrote a bill of divorce on condition, it is valid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule out of רבי יוסי's ruling on the משנה quoted in Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יוסי hold that a גט written on condition, before the condition is met, is valid in general?

steps.title: The husband's word order means 'write now'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says no. In general רבי יוסי would call it פסול, but here the husband put 'write and give' first, which means 'write now, give only if I do not come.' The רבנן do not draw any difference from word order.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really I can tell you it is invalid, but here it is different. He could have said 'If I do not come, write and give,' but he said 'Write and give if I do not come.' So he means: write now, and give if I do not come. The רבנן hold there is no difference between one way of saying it and the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects the broad rule. He explains that רבי יוסי's ruling comes from how the husband ordered his words in this specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the condition came first ('if I do not come, write and give'), it would cover both writing and giving. Since the husband said 'write and give' first, רבי יוסי reads the condition as attached only to the giving, so writing is allowed right away. The רבנן do not read meaning into word order, so for them the writing was also conditional and the גט is invalid.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי does not validate every גט written on condition. He only reads 'write and give if I do not come' as 'write now, give later.' The רבנן ignore word order.

phrases.english: No; actually I can say to you it is invalid,
and here it is different –
since he could have said:
'If I do not come, write and give';
but he said: 'Write and give if I do not come';
this is what he is saying: write from now,
and give if I do not come.
And the Rabbis – there is no difference this way
and no difference that way.
phrases.notes: For the רבנן, both word orders mean the same thing, so the writing also has to wait.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5 by limiting רבי יוסי's ruling to the husband's specific wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי generally invalidates a גט written on condition. Here, putting 'write and give' first means 'write now, give if I do not come.' The רבנן see no difference in word order.

steps.title: How much extra time 'after' adds
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'after' a time period adds time: after a seven-year cycle means a year more, after a year means a month more, after a month means a week more.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'After a seven-year cycle' means a year after it; 'after a year' means a month after it; 'after a month' means a week after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a husband who makes the גט depend on a time period with the word 'after.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'after' is not read as the very next moment. It adds a span of time that fits the size of the period mentioned. The bigger the period, the bigger the added time.
steps.confusionAlert: Here שָׁבוּעַ does not mean a week. It means a seven-year cycle. A week is called שַׁבָּת in this ברייתא.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'After a seven-year cycle' – a year;
phrases.notes: The case is a husband who says 'this is your גט if I do not come back after' this time period.

phrases.english: 'After a year' – a month;
'After a month' – a week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's time condition to a related ברייתא about time conditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'After' a period adds time: a seven-year cycle adds a year, a year adds a month, a month adds a week.

steps.title: What does 'after שבת' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a case the ברייתא left out: what if he said 'after שבת' (after a week)?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'after שבת,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the next smaller time period, which the ברייתא did not mention. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא went down from seven years, to a year, to a month. The natural next question is how far the phrase 'after שבת' reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it? / what is the law?

phrases.english: 'After Shabbat' – what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ברייתא of Step 7 to a case it did not cover.

steps.title: Sunday to Tuesday are 'after שבת'
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רבי אסי (or רבי יוחנן): Sunday, Monday and Tuesday are called 'after שבת'; Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are called 'before שבת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא sat before רבי אסי (some say רבי אסי sat before רבי יוחנן), and he said: Sunday, Monday and Tuesday are 'after שבת.' Wednesday, Thursday and Friday are 'before שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by telling how the days of the week are named in relation to שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first three days of the week still count as 'after שבת.' The last three days count as 'before שבת.' So 'after שבת' reaches up through Tuesday.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַבִּי זֵירָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira sat before Rabbi Asi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Asi sat before Rabbi Yoḥanan,
and he said: Sunday, and Monday, and Tuesday –
are after Shabbat.
Wednesday, and Thursday and Friday –
are before Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבִּי זֵירָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sunday through Tuesday count as 'after שבת'; Wednesday through Friday count as 'before שבת.'

steps.title: רבי: 'after the רגל' means thirty days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי that 'after the רגל' means thirty days after the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי says: 'After the festival' means thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another time phrase, 'after the רגל,' and רבי's view that it adds thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the pattern of Step 7, where 'after' adds a set amount of time. Here the added time for a רגל is thirty days. The next step will check whether this is the הלכה.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi says:
'After the festival' – thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another 'after' time phrase to the list from Steps 7–9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, 'after the רגל' means thirty days after the festival.

steps.title: רבי's ruling is not the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא taught the ruling in רבי's name and was praised. When he taught it as the majority view, he was not praised. This shows the הלכה does not follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא went out and taught it in רבי's name, and they praised him. He taught it in the name of the many, and they did not praise him. So the הלכה does not follow it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows from how listeners reacted that רבי's 'thirty days' ruling is not accepted as הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching it as one Sage's view was fine, so they praised it. Teaching it as the majority view would make people treat it as הלכה, and they did not praise that. From this the גמרא concludes the הלכה is not like רבי here.

keyTerms.meaning: the הלכה is not like him

steps.whatToRemember: 'After the רגל' adding thirty days is רבי's own view, and the הלכה does not follow it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya went out
and taught it in the name of Rabbi – and they praised him;
in the name of the many – and they did not praise him;
phrases.notes: 'In the name of the many' means teaching it as the general, majority view.

phrases.english: apparently, the halakha is not in accordance with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַק רַבִּי חִיָּיא דַּרְשַׁהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the הלכה regarding רבי's ruling from Step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה does not follow רבי's ruling that 'after the רגל' means thirty days.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק מי שאחזו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally closes פרק מי שאחזו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק מי שאחזו.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק called מי שאחזו. It is a closing formula, not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell said when finishing a פרק, expressing the hope to come back and learn it again. After this line a brand-new topic begins.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing formula of a פרק
'One who was seized': the name of the פרק that just ended

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'One who was seized'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק whose final discussion ended at step 11.

steps.title: New פרק: throwing a גט to one's wife
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on when a thrown גט counts as given. It works in her house or courtyard, and in her lap or basket. It does not work in his house or courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man throws a גט to his wife while she is in her house or courtyard, she is divorced. If he threw it to her inside his house or courtyard, she is not divorced, even if the גט lands right with her in the bed. If he threw it into her lap or her basket, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The new פרק opens with a משנה about throwing a גט instead of handing it over. The question is whose space the גט lands in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her house and courtyard belong to her, so a גט landing there counts as reaching her. His house and courtyard belong to him, so the גט is still in his space, even if it lands right beside her. Her lap and her basket count as hers even when she is in his house.

keyTerms.meaning: One who throws; the opening word and name of the new פרק

steps.confusionAlert: In ״אפילו הוא עמה במטה״, the word ״הוא״ means the גט, not the husband. Even though the גט is right there in the bed with her, it is in HIS house, so it does not work.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole פרק is built on the idea that a גט can reach the wife through her property or her personal space, not only through her hand.

phrases.english: One who throws a bill of divorce to his wife,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִיא בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתָהּ אוֹ בְּתוֹךְ חֲצֵרָהּ –
phrases.english: and she is in her house or in her courtyard —
she is divorced.

phrases.aramaic: זְרָקוֹ לָהּ בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ אוֹ בְּתוֹךְ חֲצֵרוֹ,
phrases.english: If he threw it to her in his house or in his courtyard,
even if it is with her in the bed —
phrases.notes: ״הוא״ here is the גט, not the husband.

phrases.english: she is not divorced.
Into her lap or into her basket —
she is divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thrown גט divorces the wife if it lands in her house, her courtyard, her lap or her basket. It does not divorce her if it lands in his house or courtyard.

steps.title: Where do we learn this from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a גט can work even when it is not placed in her hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these rules?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's ruling. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of placing the גט in her hand. So the גמרא wants to know how we know that her house or courtyard also works.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה just taught.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a גט placed in the wife's domain counts as given to her.

steps.title: The word ״ונתן״ includes her roof, courtyard and enclosure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word ״ונתן״ that a גט works when placed in her property, not only in her hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: ״ונתן בידה״ — from this I would only know her hand. How do I know her roof, her courtyard and her enclosure? The פסוק says ״ונתן״, meaning in any way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק about giving a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״בידה״ alone would limit the giving to her actual hand. The extra stress on ״ונתן״, 'he gives', teaches that any real giving counts, including into places she owns. This is the source for the משנה's 'her house or courtyard'.

keyTerms.meaning: And he gives it in her hand (דברים 24:1)
Her enclosure: a fenced area outside the house
In any case or any way

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"And he gives it in her hand" —
I have only her hand;
her roof, her courtyard and her enclosure — from where?
The verse says: "and he gives" —
in any way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״ונתן״ widens giving beyond her hand to her roof, courtyard and enclosure.

steps.title: The same idea with a thief
steps.stepSummary: A parallel ברייתא learns from ״המצא תמצא״ that a גנב is liable even when the stolen item is found on his property.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught about a גנב: ״ידו״ — from this I would only know his hand. How do I know his roof, his courtyard and his enclosure? The פסוק says ״המצא תמצא״, meaning in any way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a matching ברייתא from the laws of a גנב to show the same pattern: a person's property works like his hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the thief's hand. The doubled phrase ״המצא תמצא״ widens it to his roof, courtyard and enclosure. This backs up the idea behind the ברייתא about the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is also taught this way

steps.whatToRemember: In both a גט and theft, a person's own domain, meaning roof, courtyard or enclosure, counts like his or her hand.

phrases.english: And it is also taught this way regarding a thief:
"His hand" — I have only his hand;
phrases.notes: שמות 22:3, about the stolen item being found in the thief's hand.

phrases.english: his roof, his courtyard and his enclosure — from where?
The verse says: "if it is surely found" —
in any way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא that supports the derivation in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a person's domain counts like his or her hand.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on a גנב, learned from ״המצא תמצא״.

steps.title: Why both sources are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the גט case and the גנב case each have a special feature, so we could not learn one from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both sources are needed. If the תורה had taught only גט, we would say it works because a woman can be divorced against her will, but a גנב, who cannot be made liable against his will, maybe not. If it had taught only גנב, we would say it is because the תורה penalized him, but a גט maybe not. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two ברייתות from the last steps are not repeating each other. Each one teaches something the other could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט works even without the wife's agreement, so her property receiving it for her is easy to accept. A גנב is a case where the תורה is strict as a penalty. Each reason is special to its own case, so neither law could be carried over to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary, meaning both teachings are needed
The Merciful One (the תורה) penalized him
I might say no, it does not apply

steps.whatToRemember: A צריכא shows that two similar sources are both needed, because each case has its own special reason that does not carry over.

phrases.english: And it is necessary to teach both
For if it had taught us only about a גט,
we would say that is because she can be divorced against her will;
but a thief, who is not made liable against his will,
I might say no.
And if it had taught us only about a thief,
we would say that is because the Merciful One penalized him;
but about a גט, I might say no,
so it is necessary to teach both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the parallel גנב source from Step 16 does not make the גט source from Step 15 unnecessary.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each case has a special reason: a גט works against the wife's will, and a גנב is penalized by the תורה. So neither can be learned from the other.

steps.title: How can a wife own her own courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that a גט thrown into her חצר works, since whatever a wife acquires belongs to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her courtyard?! Whatever a woman acquires, her husband acquires!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and attacks the words "her courtyard." A married woman's property is controlled by her husband, so how can it be called hers?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her חצר can only receive a גט for her if it truly counts as hers. But the rule מה שקנתה אשה קנה בעלה gives the husband rights in her property. So the courtyard seems to be his, and a גט thrown into his property does not work, as the משנה itself said.

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever a wife acquires, her husband acquires

phrases.english: Her courtyard?!
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from Step 13, which said a גט thrown into her courtyard works.

phrases.english: Whatever a woman acquires, her husband acquires!

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲצֵרָהּ מָה שֶׁקָּנְתָה אִשָּׁה קָנָה בַּעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the source discussion, the גמרא returns to the משנה and questions the case of "her courtyard."
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a גט thrown into her חצר works
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wife's acquisitions belong to her husband, so her courtyard is really his, and a גט thrown into his property does not work.

steps.title: The husband gave up his rights to her property
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the משנה is talking about a husband who wrote that he has no claim to his wife's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The case is where he wrote to her, "I have no claim or dealings in your property."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the challenge by narrowing the משנה to a special case. Here the husband gave up his rights, so the courtyard is fully hers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the husband does have rights in his wife's property. But if he writes that he has nothing to do with her property, those rights are gone. Then the חצר counts as hers alone and can receive the גט for her.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the answer
I have no claim or dealings

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer sets up the next challenge: whether a statement like this is strong enough to give up rights at all.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:
It is where he writes to her:
"I have no claim or dealings in your property."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18 by placing the משנה in a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her courtyard belongs to her husband, so it cannot receive a גט for her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a husband who wrote that he has no claim to her property, so the courtyard is hers alone.

steps.title: Saying 'I have no claim' accomplishes nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's answer using a ברייתא that says giving up a claim with words alone has no effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: What good does it do if he writes this to her? We learned in a ברייתא that if someone tells his friend, 'I have no claim on this field,' 'I have no dealings with it,' or 'My hand is removed from it,' his words mean nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 19. If simply giving up a claim with words does nothing, the husband's note should not help either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said the husband wrote that he has no claim to his wife's property. The ברייתא shows that a statement like 'I have no claim' cannot take away rights a person already has. So the husband would still own what she acquires, and the גט in her חצר would still be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: I have no legal claim or dispute (over this)
I have no dealings with it
he has said nothing; his words have no legal effect

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי כְּתַב לַהּ הָכִי – מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: But when he writes this to her, what of it?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
One who says to his fellow:

phrases.aramaic: ״דִּין וּדְבָרִים אֵין לִי עַל שָׂדֶה זוֹ״;
phrases.english: "I have no legal claim on this field";
and "I have no dealings with it";
and "My hand is removed from it" —
he has said nothing!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי כְּתַב לַהּ הָכִי – מַאי הָוֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אלעזר's answer from Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that the husband wrote he has no claim to her property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules that a statement giving up rights to property has no effect, so the husband's note should not remove his rights either.

steps.title: He wrote it while she was only betrothed
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי answers that the husband wrote the note while she was still an ארוסה, before his rights began. This fits רב כהנא's rule about turning down an inheritance before it arrives.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי says: the case is where he wrote this to her while she was still only betrothed. This follows רב כהנא, who said that a person can make a condition ahead of time not to inherit an inheritance that comes to him from somewhere other than his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Giving up a right is effective when the right has not yet come to you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in Step 20 is about someone who already owns the field, so words cannot undo that. A husband gets rights to his wife's property only once they are fully married. If he writes the note during אירוסין, he is turning down a right before it comes to him, and רב כהנא teaches that this works.

keyTerms.meaning: a betrothed woman, before full marriage
from another place (not from his father)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up an important distinction: you cannot give away with words a right you already have, but you can turn down a right before it reaches you.

phrases.english: They say in the school of Rabbi Yannai:
It is where he writes to her while she is still betrothed,
and this follows Rav Kahana,
as Rav Kahana says:

phrases.aramaic: נַחֲלָה הַבָּאָה לוֹ לְאָדָם מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר,
phrases.english: An inheritance that comes to a person from another place,
phrases.notes: This means an inheritance that does not come from his father.

phrases.english: a person can stipulate about it that he will not inherit it;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: בְּכוֹתֵב לָהּ – וְעוֹדָהּ אֲרוּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (timing): the note was written before his rights took effect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband's note seemed to be giving up rights he already had, which the ברייתא says is useless.
steps.terutzMaskana: He wrote it during אירוסין, before his rights began, and turning down a right before it arrives works, as רב כהנא teaches.

steps.title: A second support from רבא begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to bring a second support for the answer, from a statement of רבא. The statement continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this also follows רבא, as רבא said: One who says...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by introducing a second support from רבא. His actual statement continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא's rule showed that one can turn down an inheritance in advance. The גמרא adds רבא's statement as a further support for the answer. Its contents come on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: And this follows Rava,
as Rava says: One who says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second supporting source to the answer of Step 21
